31|Primary Safety and All Efficacy
32|All confirmed efficacy events will be listed, indicating the patient id, randomized treatment
33|group, age, gender, race and day of event relative to start of dosing. The time of death and
34|cause of death will also be included in the listing of deaths.
35|4.5.1
36|Analysis of the Primary Safety/Efficacy Endpoint
37|The primary safety/efficacy endpoint is defined as the time from randomization to the onset of
38|any event in the primary composite CV endpoint (CV-related death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal
39|stroke).
40|In the unlikely event that two or more confirmed endpoints occur on the same day, the
41|following hierarchy will be used to ascribe the primary component of the composite:
42|
43|Nonfatal Myocardial infarction
44|
45|Nonfatal Stroke
46|
47|CV-related Death

6|The contribution of each component of the primary composite safety/efficacy endpoint to the
7|overall treatment effect will be examined.
8|Event rates of the primary composite CV endpoint will be estimated and Kaplan-Meier curves
9|will be plotted for the time from randomization to first occurrence of the primary composite
10|CV endpoint, by treatment group and prior CV risk at randomization based on IVRS.
11|Homogeneity of the effect of treatment on the components of the primary safety/efficacy CV
12|composite endpoint will be assessed using the method proposed by Lunn and McNeil9 (1995).
13|Briefly, this method requires augmenting the analysis dataset by including one observation per
14|component of the CV composite per subject, with an additional variable indicating the type of
15|the potential event (CV-related death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke). If a patient experienced
16|an event which counted as the first instance of the CV composite endpoint, the event status
17|for that event will be one and it will be zero for the other two types of events, which will be
18|censored at the time the first event occurred. If a patient did not have CV composite endpoint,
19|event status will be zero for all three component types of events. For example, if a patient had
20|nonfatal MI on day 270 which counted as his first occurrence of the CV composite, he would
21|have three observations in the analysis dataset: 1) type=nonfatal MI, status=1, time=270; 2)
22|type=nonfatal stroke, status=0, time=270; 3) type=CV death, status=0, time=270. The
23|augmented dataset will be analyzed using Cox regression with (time, status) as response
24|variables and event type, treatment and treatment by event type interaction as covariates. To
25|account for the use of multiple observations per subject in the analysis, Lin-Wei robust
26|sandwich variance3 will be used. The test of treatment by event type interaction will be the test
27|of homogeneity of treatment effect on the components of the CV composite endpoint. Hazard
28|ratios and 95% CIs for treatment effect on each component of the primary endpoint will be
29|produced.
30|4.5.1.1
31|Primary Safety Analysis: Non-inferiority of EQW versus Placebo
32|To determine whether EQW is non-inferior to placebo, a non-inferiority margin of 1.30 in
33|terms of hazard ratio with respect to developing the primary composite CV endpoint will be
34|used.
35|The primary safety hypothesis (H1) is defined as:
36|H0: HR ≥ 1.3 vs. H1: HR < 1.3
37|The hypothesis of non-inferiority will be tested at a one-sided significance level of 0.02495 in
38|the ITT population using a Cox Proportional Hazards model which includes treatment as
39|explanatory factor with prior CV event at randomization based on IVRS as a stratification
40|factor. The two-sided 95% confidence interval for the hazard ratio of EQW to placebo will be
41|estimated. If the upper limit of the two-sided confidence interval for the estimated HR for the
42|stratified Cox model is below the non-inferiority margin of 1.30 then non-inferiority of the

8|4.5.1.2
9|Primary Efficacy Analysis: Superiority of EQW versus Placebo
10|If the non-inferiority hypothesis is met, the hypothesis of superiority of EQW, when used in
11|addition to usual care versus usual care without EQW with regard to the risk of developing the
12|primary composite CV endpoint will be tested at a one-sided significance level of 0.02495
13|(i.e. two-sided 0.0499).
14|The efficacy hypothesis (H1) is defined as:
15|H0: HR ≥ 1 vs. H1: HR < 1
16|The Intention to Treat (ITT) population will be used to evaluate the primary efficacy
17|hypothesis. The p-value will be estimated using the same Cox Proportional Hazards model as
18|in the non-inferiority analysis . The estimated HR and two-sided 95% confidence interval for
19|the hazard ratio of EQW to placebo will also be presented.
20|The above primary safety and efficacy analyses will use the Primary Censoring Scheme (see
21|Section 4.1.2.1).
22|4.5.1.3
23|Assessment of Model Assumption
24|The assumption of proportional hazards for the factor for treatment group will be assessed
25|visually using log-cumulative hazard plots for each stratum, and with models which assess the
26|treatment effect in categorized time intervals (< 1 year, 1- <2 years, 2-<3 years, >=3 years), or
27|time-dependent covariates in the model. The effect of any departures from proportional
28|hazards will be discussed as part of the presentation of results of the analyses. If there is
29|evidence of non-proportionality appropriate further analyses using Lin-Wei information
30|sandwich3 may be conducted.
31|4.5.1.4
32|Sensitivity Analyses of the Primary Efficacy Endpoint
33|It is expected that complete information on the components of the primary composite endpoint
34|(and as much as possible of the eCRF data for patients contacted by telephone) will be
35|obtained for all patients including those who prematurely discontinue investigational product,
36|unless they refuse any form of follow-up and withdraw consent or where final status could not
37|be determined.
38|For the primary efficacy endpoint, the following sensitivity analyses will also be performed:
39|1. Analyze the data in ITT population using Primary Censoring Scheme (see Section
40|4.1.2.1) and using a Cox proportional hazards model that includes treatment as an
41|explanatory factor and prior CV risk group at randomization based on CRF data as
42|stratification variable.
